Preprocess time/wavelength data

Source: R/preprocess.R
preprocess.Rd

Standard preprocessing of time × wavelength response matrices (e.g. HPLC-DAD/UV data), consisting of: (i) optional subtraction of a reference band of wavelengths, (ii) optional interpolation in either dimension for dimensionality reduction, (iii) optional smoothing along the spectral axis, and (iv) optional baseline correction along the time axis. For densely sampled data (e.g., UV-VIS spectra), the size of the matrix can be reduced by interpolation. By default, the data are smoothed along the spectral axis using cubic smoothing splines (smooth.spline), then baseline-corrected along the time axis by asymmetric least squares (asysm). Three other baseline estimators are available through baseline, and baseline = "none" skips the step; see baseline_estimators.

Usage

preprocess(
  X,
  dim1,
  dim2,
  remove.time.baseline = NULL,
  baseline = c("als", "arpls", "aspls", "snip", "none"),
  attach_baseline = FALSE,
  zero_floor = FALSE,
  smooth_spectra = TRUE,
  reference_wavelengths = NULL,
  interpolate_rows = TRUE,
  interpolate_cols = TRUE,
  cl = 2,
  show_progress = NULL,
  outlier_cutoff = 5/60,
  ...,
  maxI = NULL,
  spec.smooth = NULL
)

Arguments

X

A numeric matrix (time × wavelength) or a list of such matrices. Row names must correspond to time points and column names to wavelengths.

dim1

Numeric vector specifying the target time grid, usually built with seq. The data will be interpolated onto these time points, which must be strictly increasing. Chromatograms that do not cover the whole of dim1 are dropped with a warning. Writing c(from, to, by = x) in place of seq(from, to, by = x) yields a three-element vector rather than a sequence, so it raises an error. If dim1 is omitted, the grid runs in steps of 0.01 (in the time units of the data) across the range shared by all chromatograms.

dim2

Numeric vector specifying the target wavelength grid, usually built with seq. The data will be interpolated onto these wavelengths, which must be strictly increasing and lie within the range of the original wavelengths; otherwise an error is raised. Ignored when interpolate_cols = FALSE. If omitted, the existing wavelengths are kept.

remove.time.baseline

The remove.time.baseline argument is deprecated. Please use baseline = "none" instead.

baseline

Baseline estimator to use along the time axis. Either asymmetric least squares ("als", the default, via asysm), asymmetrically reweighted penalized least squares ("arpls"), adaptive smoothness parameter penalized least squares ("aspls"), statistics-sensitive non-linear iterative peak-clipping ("snip"), or "none" to skip baseline correction along the time axis altogether. See baseline_estimators for a description of each.

attach_baseline

Logical. Whether to retain the estimated baseline alongside the corrected data as an "estimated_baseline" attribute. The parameter that produced it (stiffness, or m for "snip") is always recorded, as a "baseline_param" attribute, whether or not the baseline itself is kept. The baseline is subtracted either way; this argument only controls whether the estimate is kept for inspection. Defaults to FALSE: the baseline is estimated separately for each wavelength, so it is the same size as the data and retaining it roughly doubles memory use. Adding the attribute back to the returned data recovers the uncorrected matrix only when zero_floor = FALSE and maxI and reference_wavelengths are unset: clipping alters the data without altering the stored estimate, maxI rescales both by a factor derived from the clipped data, and the subtracted reference band is not stored.

zero_floor

Logical. Whether to clip negative values in the corrected data to zero. Defaults to FALSE. Clipping discards the half of the noise that falls below zero, which hides the negative dips that show where a baseline was over-subtracted, so it is turned off by default.

smooth_spectra

Logical, indicating whether smoothing should be done along the spectral axis, according to smooth.spline. Skipped for data with fewer than four wavelengths. Defaults to TRUE.

reference_wavelengths

Numeric vector of length 2 giving a band of wavelengths, c(from, to), whose mean is subtracted from every wavelength at each time point, like the reference wavelength of a diode-array detector. This removes offsets shared by all wavelengths, such as lamp drift or refractive-index effects, before the baseline is estimated. Choose a band where nothing in the samples absorbs. Either bound may be NA to leave that side open. Defaults to NULL (no subtraction).

interpolate_rows

Logical. Whether to interpolate along the time axis (dim1). Defaults to TRUE.

interpolate_cols

Logical. Whether to interpolate along the spectral axis (dim2). Defaults to TRUE.

cl

Either an integer specifying the number of cores to use for parallel processing or a cluster object created by makeCluster. Defaults to 2. On Windows integer values will be ignored.

show_progress

Logical. Whether to show progress bar. Defaults to TRUE if pbapply is installed.

outlier_cutoff

Threshold (in minutes) for excluding chromatograms that end earlier than expected. Samples ending more than this value before the median end time are removed with a warning. The value is always in minutes, whatever time unit the chromatograms are stored in. Defaults to 5/60, i.e. 5 seconds. Only applies when dim1 is not specified.

...

Additional arguments to the selected baseline estimator: e.g. stiffness and p for "als" (asysm), stiffness for "arpls", stiffness and k for "aspls", or m (required) for "snip". Because maxI follows ... in the signature, it must be named in full: an abbreviation such as max is passed to the estimator, which rejects it.

maxI

If supplied, each chromatogram is rescaled so that its maximum intensity equals maxI.

spec.smooth

The spec.smooth argument is deprecated. Please use smooth_spectra instead.

Value

The function returns the preprocessed data matrix (or list of matrices), with row names and column names indicating the time points and wavelengths, respectively.

Details

The operations are applied in the order given above: reference subtraction first, on the original wavelengths, then interpolation, then spectral smoothing, then baseline correction. Because the baseline is estimated after the time axis is interpolated, stiffness is tied to whichever dim1 grid was chosen: the penalty applies on the index axis, so the same value gives a different baseline on a differently sampled grid. Choose dim1 first, then tune stiffness against that grid.

Note

Adapted from the preprocess function in the alsace package by Ron Wehrens: https://github.com/rwehrens/alsace/blob/master/R/preprocess.R.

References

  • Baek, S.-J., Park, A., Ahn, Y.-J., and Choo, J. 2015. Baseline correction using asymmetrically reweighted penalized least squares smoothing. Analyst 140:250-257. doi:10.1039/C4AN01061B .

  • Zhang, F., Tang, X., Tong, A., Wang, B., Wang, J., Lv, Y., Tang, C., and Wang, J. 2020. Baseline correction for infrared spectra using adaptive smoothness parameter penalized least squares method. Spectroscopy Letters 53:222-233. doi:10.1080/00387010.2020.1730908 .

  • Ryan, C.G., Clayton, E., Griffin, W.L., Sie, S.H., and Cousens, D.R. 1988. SNIP, a statistics-sensitive background treatment for the quantitative analysis of PIXE spectra in geoscience applications. Nuclear Instruments and Methods in Physics Research B 34:396-402. doi:10.1016/0168-583X(88)90063-8 .

  • Erb, D. 2025. pybaselines: A Python library of algorithms for the baseline correction of experimental data. doi:10.5281/zenodo.5608581 .

Author

Examples

data(Sa)
new.ts <- seq(10,18.66,by=.01) # choose time-points
new.lambdas <- seq(200, 318, by = 2) # choose wavelengths
Sa_pr <- preprocess(Sa[[1]], dim1 = new.ts, dim2 = new.lambdas)
